printed: At 60 m/s, spinning 20 rad/s: a step a frame finds it in the wall at frame 5 (0.0833 s); conservative advancement finds it touching at 0.0826 s, in 12 steps.
At 80 m/s, spinning 15 rad/s: a step a frame never finds it in the wall; conservative advancement finds it touching at 0.0611 s, in 11 steps.

Credits: conservative advancement is Brian Mirtich's (1996); a frame's motion as one turn about a point, Michel Chasles' theorem (1830); that turn as a motor of projective geometric algebra, Charles Gunn's (2011), written as Steven De Keninck's ganja.js does.
